description:
Exclude history files from `jit search` when no file selection is given, using one declaration of the history paths.

## Background

`jit search` with no `--glob` runs ripgrep over the whole data root (`crates/jit/src/search.rs`, CLI call site in `main.rs`), so it reads the event log and every gate-run record. The server always passes explicit globs and is unaffected. `search()` runs ripgrep with its working directory at the data root and matches globs relative to it. Verified on ripgrep 15.2.0: anchored negations exclude all three history paths, result paths stay absolute, and an explicit glob still reaches a gate-run file. An unanchored `!tmp` would also hide any nested `tmp`, so the exclusions are anchored. The redo scratch directory can hold appended event bytes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `repository_state/path.rs` declares the data-root history paths (the event log, the gate-run directory and the redo scratch directory) once, beside their `VirtualPath` constants.
- [hard] REQ-02: When neither a glob nor explicit file patterns are given, the search excludes each declared history path by an anchored negation; an explicit selection is passed through unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A unit test over a corpus shows that a default search returns no match from a history file, that a same-named file nested elsewhere is still searched, and that an explicit glob still reaches a history file.
title: Default search reads no history file
